Sales Median asking price 1 bed $899K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,650 Bisected by Flatbush Avenue and bordered by the BQE, Downtown Brooklyn is a rapidly expanding residential neighborhood. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. Sales Median asking price 2 beds $1.3M Rentals Median asking base rent 2 beds $4,999 When George Washington commandeered the building site that would eventually become Gracie Mansion, he probably didn't imagine that this peaceful, riverside enclave would become the lively residential neighborhood it is today. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Sales Median asking price 2 beds $1.3M Rentals Median asking base rent 2 beds $5,000 When George Washington commandeered the building site that would eventually become Gracie Mansion, he probably didn't imagine that this peaceful, riverside enclave would become the lively residential neighborhood it is today. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Sales Median asking price 2 beds $1.65M Rentals Median asking base rent 2 beds $5,400 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $950K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,325 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Log in Explore Boerum Hill TRANSIT SCHOOLS COLLEGES PARKS MUSEUMS Transit Location Distance Rat Union St 0.27 miles BDNQR2345at Atlantic Av–Barclays Ctr 0.3 miles 23at Bergen St 0.4 miles LIRRat Atlantic Terminal 0.43 miles 2345at Nevins St 0.5 miles View transit on Google Maps View on Google Maps About Boerum Hill Sales Median asking price 2 beds $1.62M Rentals Median asking base rent 2 beds $5,325 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Sales Median asking price 2 beds $1.65M Rentals Median asking base rent 2 beds $5,400 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $899K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,650 Bisected by Flatbush Avenue and bordered by the BQE, Downtown Brooklyn is a rapidly expanding residential neighborhood. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $899K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,650 Bisected by Flatbush Avenue and bordered by the BQE, Downtown Brooklyn is a rapidly expanding residential neighborhood. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $899K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,650 Bisected by Flatbush Avenue and bordered by the BQE, Downtown Brooklyn is a rapidly expanding residential neighborhood. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $950K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,325 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $925K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,395 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $899K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,650 Bisected by Flatbush Avenue and bordered by the BQE, Downtown Brooklyn is a rapidly expanding residential neighborhood. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $950K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,325 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Log in Explore Boerum Hill Transit Schools Colleges Parks Museums Transit Location Distance R at Union St 0.31 miles B D N Q R 2 3 4 5 at Atlantic Av–Barclays Ctr 0.33 miles F G at Bergen St 0.44 miles A C G at Hoyt & Schermerhorn 0.46 miles 2 3 at Bergen St 0.47 miles View transit on Google Maps View on Google Maps About Boerum Hill Sales Median asking price 2 beds $1.6M Rentals Median asking base rent 2 beds $5,325 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Sales Median asking price 2 beds $1.3M Rentals Median asking base rent 2 beds $5,000 When George Washington commandeered the building site that would eventually become Gracie Mansion, he probably didn't imagine that this peaceful, riverside enclave would become the lively residential neighborhood it is today. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Log in Explore Yorkville TRANSIT SCHOOLS COLLEGES PARKS MUSEUMS Transit Location Distance Qat 96th St 0.17 miles Qat 86th St 0.25 miles 456at 86th St 0.38 miles 6at 96th St 0.38 miles 6at 103rd St 0.67 miles View transit on Google Maps View on Google Maps About Yorkville Sales Median asking price 1 bed $699K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $3,800 When George Washington commandeered the building site that would eventually become Gracie Mansion, he probably didn't imagine that this peaceful, riverside enclave would become the lively residential neighborhood it is today. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Fans of new construction will find new condo developments too. Saint Marks Place, The Hendrick, The Boerum, and The Bergen have expanded buyers' opportunities. Renters will also find plenty of options here in a broad range of prices, from the genuinely affordable to the luxurious. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $699K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $3,895 When George Washington commandeered the building site that would eventually become Gracie Mansion, he probably didn't imagine that this peaceful, riverside enclave would become the lively residential neighborhood it is today. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block.
